# Sourdough levain

A levain is a portion of the sourdough starter built up the night before baking, so the bread dough gets a vigorous dose of wild yeast. Mix it into the dough when it peaks; see [[Proofing dough]] for the rise that follows.

Mix 20 g of ripe starter with 100 g of flour and 100 g of water and leave it covered for eight to twelve hours at room temperature.

The levain is ready when it has doubled, its surface is domed and bubbly, and it smells sweet and tangy rather than sharp.

Like [[Cheese cultures]], a levain relies on lactic acid bacteria to sour and flavour what they feed on.
